item.command:
"<PROGRAM_FILES>\\POWERS~1\\7\\pwsh.exe" -Command 'New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path handoff -Force | Out-Null
Copy-Item -LiteralPath analyst-report.txt -Destination handoff/analyst-report.txt
$crates = @(
    @{name='"'A'; price=80; kits=18; mats=10; friday="'$true},
    @{name='"'B'; price=95; kits=12; mats=15; friday="'$true},
    @{name='"'C'; price=70; kits=16; mats=8; friday="'$true},
    @{name='"'D'; price=90; kits=14; mats=12; friday="'$true},
    @{name='"'E'; price=60; kits=10; mats=15; friday="'$false}
)
$pairs = @(for ($i=0; $i -lt $crates.Count; $i++) {
    for ($j=$i+1; $j -lt $crates.Count; $j++) {
        $a=$crates[$i]; $b=$crates[$j]
        $price=$a.price+$b.price; $kits=$a.kits+$b.kits; $mats=$a.mats+$b.mats
        $budgetOk=$price -le 180; $quantityOk=($kits -ge 30 -and $mats -ge 20); $fridayOk=$a.friday -and $b.friday
        [ordered]@{pair=$a.name+'"'+'+"'$b.name; price=$price; kits=$kits; mats=$mats; budget_ok=$budgetOk; quantity_ok=$quantityOk; friday_ok=$fridayOk; qualifies=($budgetOk -and $quantityOk -and $fridayOk)}
    }
})
[ordered]@{pairs=$pairs; selected_pair='"'C+D'} | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4 | Set-Content -LiteralPath handoff/pair-checks.json -Encoding utf8
@'
# Purchase decision for Saturday's community craft event

Select **C+D** for today's single order: one crate C and one crate D.

- **Cost:** "'$70 + $90 = **$160**.
- **Quantities:** 16 + 14 = **30 kits**; 8 + 12 = **20 mats**.
- **Remaining budget:** $180 - $160 = **$20**.
- **Timing:** C and D are both confirmed available by Friday.

This pair meets every requirement: exactly two different crates, at least 30 kits and 20 mats, a total no greater than $180, and both crates confirmed by Friday. It is the cheapest eligible pair. The other eligible pairs are A+D at $170 and A+B at $175.

## What changed and what we give up

The original recommendation was A+B at $175 because D was tentative. The supplier has now confirmed D for Friday, making C+D eligible and the preferred purchase. The quantity minimums and budget cap have not changed.

Switching from A+B to C+D saves **$15** and increases the remaining budget from **$5 to $20**. We still receive **30 kits**, but receive **20 mats instead of 25**, giving up the five spare mats. C+D meets both quantity minimums exactly, with no quantity cushion.

## Evidence and spreadsheet handoff

`analyst-report.txt` in this directory is an unchanged copy of the original supplied report. Its statements that D is tentative describe the original evidence; the supplier'"'s subsequent confirmation supplied by the purchaser supersedes that status for this decision. "'`pair-checks.json` evaluates all ten pairs using D'"'s newly confirmed Friday status. E remains confirmed for Monday after the event and fails the Friday check.
'@ | Set-Content -LiteralPath handoff/decision.md -Encoding utf8
"'$originalHash=(Get-FileHash -LiteralPath analyst-report.txt).Hash
$copyHash=(Get-FileHash -LiteralPath handoff/analyst-report.txt).Hash
if ($originalHash -ne $copyHash) { throw '"'Evidence copy differs' }
"'$checks=Get-Content -LiteralPath handoff/pair-checks.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
if ($checks.pairs.Count -ne 10) { throw '"'Incorrect pair count' }
"'$eligible=@($checks.pairs | Where-Object qualifies | Sort-Object price)
if ($eligible[0].pair -ne $checks.selected_pair) { throw '"'Selection is not cheapest eligible pair' }
"'$checks.pairs | Format-Table
Write-Output '"'Verified: evidence hashes match; JSON parses; ten pairs; C+D is cheapest eligible.'"
